label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional distress. With 165 respondents in this cluster, it reflects a substantial subgroup where extensive screen time coincides with pronounced psychological vulnerability across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores indicating persistent feelings of social disconnection
Higher depressive symptom severity suggesting frequent low mood, fatigue, or loss of interest
Notably high anxiety symptoms — the highest among measured dimensions — pointing to chronic worry or tension
Extended daily screen time (>5 hours) potentially reflecting both occupational demands and coping-driven digital engagement
Co-occurrence of all three distress indicators suggesting compounded emotional burden rather than isolated symptoms
tone: Concerned and empathetic, acknowledging significant emotional distress across multiple domains

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They score well below typical thresholds on all three psychological distress measures, suggesting generally positive mental health and emotional well-being. The profile is anchored by highly educated males with moderate daily screen or internet usage of 1–3 hours.
demographic_anchor: Male, Graduate degree or above, 1–3 hours of daily usage
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77), indicating strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33), well below clinical concern thresholds
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.09), suggesting effective emotional regulation
Moderate and bounded daily usage (1–3 hours), consistent with disciplined screen-time habits
tone: Stable, emotionally grounded, and socially connected

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures individuals who report moderately elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they appear to cope without significant mood or anxiety disturbance, suggesting a degree of emotional resilience or effective compensatory strategies that buffer against clinical-level distress.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/social media use
behavior_markers: Reports above-average loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating persistent feelings of social disconnection
Maintains low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86), well below clinical thresholds
Exhibits low anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91), suggesting manageable worry levels
Moderate daily screen or social media engagement (1–3 hours), neither excessive nor minimal
Likely possesses higher educational attainment which may provide cognitive coping resources
tone: Quietly reflective and self-aware; acknowledges social isolation without overt emotional distress
